newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale okays emergency harvest funds.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale okays emergency harvest funds.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale on Monday approved emergency funds to farmers in the western Prairies who were not able to harvest their wheat or barley due to cold, wet weather, Goodale's spokesman said.
"The Minister agreed to it and once he has agreed he authorizes the (Canadian) Wheat Board to make the emergency advance payments," Goodale spokesman Vern Greenshields said.
By law the funds could not be approved before Nov 15.
Ninety-six percent of crops were harvested in Alberta and Saskatchewan and all crops were in the bin in Manitoba, Greenshields said.
The funds allow payments of up to C$15,000 a farmer for unharvested wheat and barley, C$3,000 a farmer to dry grain.
The emergency fund was last invoked in 1993, the CWB said.
